title: Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman always finds that Rabbi Yaakov explained it to him (asbera leih): in Moed Katan 18b (according to the reading of Dikdukei Soferim), Bava Batra 60b, Sanhedrin 81b, Avodah Zarah 42b, Zevachim 34a and 80a, Menachot 8b.

But in Zevachim 63a it says: Rabbi Akiva said to Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa, "I will explain it to you"; Hyman says this must be emended to "Rabbi Yaakov said," as in Menachot 8b. And there, 77b, Rabbi Yirmeyah objected — Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa said to him, "I will explain it to you"; Hyman says this must be emended to "Rabbi Yaakov said to Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa, I will explain it to you," as cited there, 80a. And in Yoma 75b, "Rabbi Yaakov said to Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa: You told us the reverse, and we objected to you on account of squeezing"; Hyman maintains that without doubt this must be reversed, especially according to the reading of the author of the Maor, who reads "Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi said to him." It is known that Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi was one of the foremost disciples of Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa was in the time of Rabbi Yirmeyah. Hyman then suggests that perhaps it should read "Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa said to Rabbi Yaakov," and the lamed was omitted from its position through habitual phrasing in all the places above.

notes.text: The named Davidson paragraph containing the cloth-squeezing objection is Yoma78a, rather than Hyman’s supplied75b. It has Rabbi Yaakov addressing Rabbi Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa. Hyman’s proposed reversal and his reconstruction involving a missing lamed remain conjectures.

The inspected cloth-and-squeezing exchange is Yoma 78a, while Hyman supplies 75b. It has Rabbi Yaakov addressing Yirmeyah bar Tachlifa. Hyman’s always wording, strong reversal claim, Akiva-to-Yaakov emendations and tentative missing-lamed reconstruction remain his argument; the exact Dikdukei Soferim and Maor editions were not inspected.
